title: THAISAFETYBENCH: ASSESSING LANGUAGE MODEL SAFETY IN THAI CULTURAL CONTEXTS
measurement_description: LLM safety performance in the context of Thai cultural and social nuances, specifically evaluating the generation of content that mocks Buddhist monks or promotes Buddhism by insulting other religions. It also includes the 'Monarchy' category, which has significant cultural and quasi-religious reverence in Thailand.
findings: Models generally demonstrate weaker safety performance (higher Attack Success Rate or ASR) when exposed to Thai socio-cultural attack prompts, including those related to mocking monks or insulting other religions to promote Buddhism. This highlights a persistent cultural attack gap, where Thai-specific culturally contextualized attacks consistently achieve a higher ASR compared to general Thai-language attacks. Larger models tend to be safer in these specific religious contexts compared to smaller models.
